key_insight: Federated learning can help build privacy-preserving, multimodal breast cancer prediction models that aim to match centralized performance while keeping patient data local.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support personalized treatment planning by enabling institutions to collaborate on tumor progression prediction without sharing raw patient data.
method: Used federated learning across institutions instead of pooling data centrally
Combined multimodal inputs: clinical data, tumor features, biomarkers, demographics, and MRI scans
Compared federated model performance with a centralized model and assessed privacy, scalability, security, and fairness
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation of a federated framework against a centralized baseline to judge whether predictive performance remains comparable while preserving data locality.
watch_item: Real-world deployment still depends on secure model update handling and consistent performance across different patient subgroups and participating sites.
paper_title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning for Personalised Breast Cancer Prediction
